tags.qa_note: Re-audit corrected outdated manta-encounter claims. Current tofoscuba.com listing and Marine Megafauna Foundation research (cited via blog.padi.com) show manta sightings have declined 88% in the first decade of monitoring and up to 99% in the second decade at Tofo cleaning stations; current sighting rate is approximately 15% of dives, not the ~80% figure previously stated. Distance from Tofo corrected from 6 km to ~15-16 km (tofoscuba.com and liquiddiveadventures.com both report this range). Cleaning station count corrected from three to two per tofoscuba.com's current listing.

Re-audit found source conflict on wall length: accommodationmozambique.co.za reports 'more than 350 metres' north-south, while tofoscuba.com's current listing describes the wall as running 'two kilometres.' Depth is roughly consistent across sources (26m to low-30s). Distance from Tofo also varies: liquiddiveadventures.com reports 3 km/5-10 min while tofoscuba.com and accommodationmozambique.co.za report 6 km/10 min. Both conflicts are noted in the markdown rather than resolved by guessing.

Re-audited 2026-08-15: re-pulled tofoscuba.com/salon; depth, distance, and species list confirmed consistent with prior entry. Added several species (honeycomb whiptail rays, leopard rays, stone fish) newly confirmed on the current page.
Re-audited 2026-08-15: re-pulled tofoscuba.com/sherwood; depth, coral type, cleaning station, and species claims all confirmed consistent with prior entry. No corrections needed.

Coordinates -23.8417/35.5875 place this site near Tofo, but Doodles is a well-documented reef at Ponta do Ouro (~-26.8, 32.9). Coordinate mismatch retained from curated data — requires correction. Re-audit 2026-08-15 reconfirmed the Ponta do Ouro location and species list against two additional independent sources (blog.padi.com, wannadive.net); also found the site is described as featuring caves and sink holes, added to markdown.

COORDINATE/NAME CONFLICT: 'Two Mile Reef' is documented in multiple sources as a reef in the Bazaruto Archipelago between Benguerra and Bazaruto Islands (~-21.8, 35.5), NOT at Ponta do Ouro. Current coordinates (-26.8333, 32.9) place this site at Ponta do Ouro where no site named 'Two Mile Reef' is confirmed. Ragged-tooth shark claim in existing description is unverified. Site cannot be validated until name/location conflict is resolved. Re-checked 2026-08-15: conflict persists; depth reports for the actual Bazaruto reef now range 6-21m (mozambique.co.za) to 6-22m (mozambiquetravel.com) across sources — noted as a minor range discrepancy, not resolved by picking one figure.

Re-audited 2026-08-15: re-pulled xray-mag.com's Ponta do Ouro feature; depth (29-50m), shark species (bull, hammerhead, tiger, 19 total species documented in the area), and cleaning-station manta visits all reconfirmed consistent with prior entry. No corrections needed.

Some sources describe Bass City as having a sunken fishing trawler forming an artificial reef element alongside the natural rocky reef. Site type kept as 'reef' since the primary character is rocky reef with potato bass aggregations, but the wreck element exists. Re-audit 2026-08-15 reconfirmed depth (16-22m), potato bass/cleaning station claims, and blue-spotted/marble electric ray claims against an additional independent source. Note: mozambique.co.za's current listing uses 'zebra shark' rather than 'leopard shark' for the same species (Stegostoma tigrinum is known by both common names in different regions) — not treated as a conflict.

Re-audit 2026-08-15: mozambique.co.za's current listing caps visibility at 'as far as 30 metres, especially in winter months' rather than the previously stated 30-40m range. Markdown softened to match current source language. Dugong and shark (Zambezi, hammerhead, silvertip) claims reconfirmed as regional/archipelago-level characteristics, consistent with prior treatment.

Insufficient site-specific sources. One source mentions San Sebastian in the context of walls, caves, and overhangs suitable for Open Water divers near Bazaruto — which conflicts with the Tofo coordinates here. Could not find 3 independent sources confirming this specific site at these coordinates. Re-checked 2026-08-15: fresh search reconfirms San Sebastian is documented as a Bazaruto-area mainland peninsula site (Amphitheatre/Caves/San Sebastian, walls to ~30m), distinct from these Tofo coordinates. Still only 2 sources and a location conflict — remains unvalidated.

Re-audit 2026-08-15: diveguinjata.com's current site listing groups sites somewhat differently than at last review (named local reefs include Turtle Creek, Batfish, Honeycomb, Fishbowl, Devil's Peak, Levi's Ledge, Caves, Pao, Hard Rock, Eel Alley, Paindane X-Press, Egypt, Coral Gardens). Exact site-count-per-category is inconsistently reported across fetches of the same page; markdown softened to avoid over-precise counts while keeping the confirmed named sites and depths.

No source confirms a site specifically named 'Quirimbas Reef'. The Quirimbas Archipelago has many named sites (Zala Bank, Rush Hour, Medjumbe walls, Neptune's Arm, etc.) but none called 'Quirimbas Reef'. This appears to be a generic curated placeholder name. Additionally, one major operator (Original Diving) notes northern Mozambique is 'off limits' due to security concerns. Cannot validate with fewer than 3 sources for this specific site name. Re-checked 2026-08-15: fresh search of Zala Bank, Rush Hour, and Medjumbe sites reconfirms none is named 'Quirimbas Reef'; still only 2 sources for this placeholder name. Remains unvalidated.
